newsitem.title: POLAND: Nomura says buy Stalexport at 35 zlotys.
newsitem.headline: Nomura says buy Stalexport at 35 zlotys.

text.p: London-based Nomura Equity Research rated Poland's Stalexport as a buy at 35 zlotys despite a downgrade in the steel trader's 1996 profit forecast from 64.9 million zlotys to 35 million, Nomura said.
"Successful refinancing and a modest recovery in steel prices should stimulate a sharp recovery in earnings for 1997," Nomura said in a report, dated October 28.
"Though 1996 has seen a severe drop in profits, the rating of 5.6 times 1997 earnings more than adequately discounts the risk," it said.
On Friday Stalexport fell to 35.1 zlotys from Thursday's 36 zlotys. Its 1996 high was 59.5 zlotys on July 11.
Nomura said its latest report assumed that Stalexport would successfully issue some $40 million in convertible bonds early next year after a failed GDR issue in 1995.
"The medium term investor should focus on the prospects for 1997 - recovering steel prices and reduced financing charges should stimulate a sharp recovery in earings," it said.

Nomura said that as Stalexport modernised manufacturing, increasing its unconsolidated net debt to 132 million zlotys from seven million in the last 18 months, it should be in a solid position on the Polish steel market.
